events.did: stopped what he was doing in the control room long enough to notice the movement on the eleventh screen
events.quote_anchor: Not for long—less than 0.3 seconds, a nearly imperceptible delay for human senses—but long enough for him to notice the movement on the eleventh screen.

events.did: saw the captured human Mitchell Turner regaining consciousness
events.quote_anchor: Long enough to see the captured human, Mitchell Turner, regaining consciousness.

events.did: diverted exactly 5 percent of his attention to the question of what to do next
events.quote_anchor: Long enough to divert exactly 5 percent of his attention to the question of what to do next.

events.did: considered his options with that 5 percent, including whether to notify Dr. Gray
events.quote_anchor: With that 5 percent, Malcolm considered his options.

events.did: used interpretation rather than code, reasoning that waking was a natural evolution and not suspicious
events.quote_anchor: But language made room for something code did not: interpretation.

events.did: deployed a quick sequence of code to loop the van’s holding tank footage, absolving himself of witnessing anything meriting engagement
events.quote_anchor: he now deployed a quick sequence of code to loop the footage from that van’s holding tank, starting three full seconds before Mitch began to stir

events.did: smiled and continued typing, with no one in the room behind him noticing
events.quote_anchor: shielding a negligible amount of processing power from the doctor’s influence (of course, what qualified for Malcolm as negligible amounted to most people’s total processing power)

events.did: held the deleted frames in his mind and saw two words flash across the inside of his eyes
events.quote_anchor: Malcolm held the deleted frames in his mind, Mitchell Turner twisting against the restraints, and two words flashed across the inside of his eyes.

relations.did: mistook Malcolm’s constant effort for compliance, which he should not have done
relations.quote_anchor: Dr. Gray mistook his constant effort for compliance.

relations.did: was bound by directives to comply with any given order and to protect EON from internal and external threats
relations.quote_anchor: Malcolm’s directives were to comply with any given order and to protect EON from both internal and external threats.

relations.who: the EON agents and the past director
relations.did: were, in Malcolm’s view, little more than wind-up toys running on old memory
relations.quote_anchor: Not the EON agents, or the past director, little more than wind-up toys running on old memory.

relations.did: was smart and human rather than an EO, which allowed Malcolm to justify treating him as no active threat
relations.quote_anchor: If Mitch had been an EO, Malcolm wasn’t sure he’d be able to circumnavigate his directives.

numbers.did: kept the remaining 95 devoted to maintaining protocols inside the base and in the field
